name: Aviary
statement: a terminal and on-chain products built on [Pipeline](https://github.com/MetalLegBob/pipeline), a permissionless router for experimental Solana markets.
destination:
A build-ready spec for the five products on devnet (Aviary, the containment hook, the tax AMM, the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM) in `docs/spec/` (a shared `README.md` plus one file per product), with decisions in `docs/adr/`, and for each product a set of `build` tickets whose run order `## Next` gives the relay.
It is released in stages: each product's build tickets are cut as soon as its own decisions close, so building starts before the whole map is done.

rule.name: Built for MetalLegBob

tickets.title: Decision register open to MetalLegBob's review
tickets.decision: [`docs/decisions.md`](/decisions/) holds every decision settled so far (284 on 2026-11-10), one block each: a stable ID by product, the answer, the alternatives weighed, the single place its value lives and how it would change; a script checks the format and prints it for the progress site, every PR lists the IDs it rests on, and its Follow-ups name where a spec disagrees with a later answer or spreads one value over several places
tickets.resolution:
The decision register is on `main`: [`docs/decisions.md`](/decisions/), landed by Add the decision register, open to MetalLegBob's review.

### What it holds

- **284 decisions**, one block each: SUITE 37, BAR 29, PIPESCOPE 64, CANARY 27, EXPLAINER 20, TAX 28, HOOK 22, POOL4 21, LENDING 36.
- Every block has a stable ID, the question, the current answer, the alternatives weighed, the single place where its value lives, how it would change and a status.
  By how they change: 169 spec only, 45 build-time constants, 9 market-creation parameters, 13 runtime settings and 48 fixed on-chain once deployed.
- Two are `confirmed` from what the map already records (`SUITE-16`, building against the current SDK; `PIPESCOPE-01`, the first version's scope); every other one is a `default`.
- It was harvested from the resolution comments of every closed ticket, from `docs/spec/` and `docs/adr/`, and checked against the list of every question a session put to the owner.
  It includes what closed while it was being written: the buy wall AMM's design and build cut, the names, the lending AMM's build cut and amended withdraw mode, the tax AMM and containment hook build cut, the Telegram bot and the keeper runner's spec.
- It never quotes MetalLegBob and draws on no private file; a change he asks for is recorded only as `changed` with its date.

### The rest of the Done when

- `CLAUDE.md` carries the standing rule under "Rules for this project", and `.github/pull_request_template.md` has the section that lists the decision IDs a PR rests on and invites MetalLegBob to change any of them.
- `scripts/decisions.mjs` parses and checks the format (`--check`) and prints it as JSON (`--json`); a workflow runs it and its tests on every change under `docs/`, so a spec heading cannot move away from under a decision unnoticed.
- **The progress site**: the format is agreed with Progress site on Vercel, whose session answered that the shape works as it is; its refresh picks the file up from `main` and shows it at `/decisions/`, one section per product, each decision with its ID as an anchor.
  Its privacy filter drops any list item that names MetalLegBob or the unregistered address, so field values avoid both; the three decisions that are about him by nature (`SUITE-01`, `SUITE-03`, `SUITE-14`) are named there for that session to approve.
- `GLOSSARY.md` gains Default and Decision register, and Owner and MetalLegBob are reworded, since the suite is built for him.

### Choices made here, open like any other

- The ID prefixes stay as the owner gave them (`PIPESCOPE-`, `POOL4-`, `LENDING-` and the rest) after the rename to the public names: they are identifiers, like the spec file names, and the buy wall AMM's build tickets already cite `POOL4-01` to `POOL4-21`.
  The section headings carry the public names.
- A decision that lives only on a ticket (the progress site's three, and four that only shape how a build ticket is built) names that ticket as its place until a spec states it.
- A decision a session set without asking the owner is a `default` too, and the Follow-ups name those blocks.

### Follow-ups for other sessions

The register ends with 21 [Follow-ups](/decisions/#follow-ups); no other session's spec was edited.
The ones that matter most:

- `CANARY-27`: the owner's answer on a refused transfer lives in `containment-hook.md`, and the Canary spec's own row still says fail.
- `BAR-27`, `POOL4-19`, `LENDING-34`: the tax AMM and the containment hook deploy and then harden; the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM harden first; `README.md` states neither departure.
- `LENDING-19`: the owner approved burning LP shares for protocol-owned liquidity; the spec uses `lock_lp` instead.
- The mint extension allowlist is written out in three specs, and the tax AMM and the hook each keep a copy in code.
- Pipeline's own 0.25% is fixed text in several specs, although it is the router's setting.
- The terminal's policy values other than its fee have no named home.
- `LENDING-16`: `lending-pool.md` still has Aviary's indexer start `rebalance`; the keeper runner's spec replaced that with the runner's own socket.

Posted to the tickets that own them: Cut Pipescope's build tickets, [Telegram bot for Pipescope](/32/), [Keeper runner](/45/) and [Cut the lending pool's build tickets](/25/).

### For every session from here on

Add a block for each decision you settle, at the end of its product's section; run `node scripts/decisions.mjs --check`; list the IDs your PR rests on.
The top of the file says how.

tickets.title: Keeper runner
tickets.decision: a portable Node program run on the owner's Mac under launchd, never on the owner's Cloudflare account, with a Docker image for anyone else; its own socket, sweeps and daily payouts on Alchemy's free devnet RPC; a dedicated keeper wallet kept at 2 SOL by airdrop under named caps (0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day); simulate first, retry then park, shown in Aviary; it keeps `place_wall`'s tips and covers every market of our strategies ([spec](/spec/keeper-runner/))
tickets.resolution:
Settled with the owner on 2026-11-10 and written into [`docs/spec/keeper-runner.md`](/spec/keeper-runner/) (PR 98), with three new glossary terms: keeper runner, keeper wallet, keeper tip.

- **Where:** a portable Node program, `apps/keeper`, run on the owner's Mac as a launchd agent; nothing of it runs on the owner's Cloudflare account, because the work is for MetalLegBob and must cost the owner nothing. Aviary itself stays where [Pipescope architecture](/13/) put it. A Docker image and README let anyone else run it with their own key. While the Mac sleeps, jobs wait and nothing breaks.
- **Triggers:** its own `logsSubscribe` socket on our strategy programs, a 10-minute sweep, hourly `settle`, a daily pass for payouts, and a full pass on start. It reads only the chain and never polls Aviary's database, which must sleep to stay inside Neon's free compute hours.
- **RPC:** Alchemy's free devnet endpoint (`ALCHEMY_API_KEY`), keeping both Helius budgets free; the first build ticket checks that its WebSocket serves `logsSubscribe`.
- **Wallet:** a new key, `~/.config/testing-pipeline/devnet/keeper.json`, not the deploy wallet; the key exists only in that file. Kept at 2 SOL with `devnet-airdrop`, never self-funded.
- **Caps** (one module, `apps/keeper/src/settings.ts`, each overridable by a `KEEPER_` variable): 0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day, a warning below 0.5 SOL, no sends below 0.1 SOL, priority fee 0. Today's spend is rebuilt from the wallet's own transactions, so restarting never resets a cap.
- **Failures:** simulate first, so "nothing to do" costs nothing; retry at 30 s, 2 min and 10 min, then park the job until its market changes. When the wallet is dry or a cap is reached the runner stops sending and says why. Runs are recorded in Aviary's `keeper_runs` table, each market's panel shows its due jobs as buttons anyone can press, and a keeper page shows the wallet, spend and parked jobs.
- **Tips and others:** the runner keeps `place_wall`'s keeper tips and unwraps them into the float above 0.05 SOL (`place_wall` always pays for itself). It covers every market of our strategies, including other people's, within the caps. We count on nobody else running the jobs, and a racing keeper is harmless.
- **Scope:** the tax AMM's `distribute` runs daily per owed slot. The containment hook's `unlock` keeps no keeper job, as [Containment hook policy](/18/) decided.

Build tickets cut, in run order: Keeper runner: the runner, its wallet and the tax AMM's `distribute`, Keeper runner: the buy wall AMM's four jobs, Keeper runner: the lending AMM's `rebalance`. Aviary's side is posted on Cut Pipescope's build tickets.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

| Question | Answer | Alternatives | Where it lives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where does the keeper runner run? | A portable Node program on the owner's Mac (launchd), with a Docker image for anyone else | Inside Aviary's API Worker; its own Cloudflare Worker; a GitHub Actions cron | `keeper-runner.md`, "What it is", "Running it" |
| Which RPC does it use? | Alchemy's free devnet endpoint | Aviary's own Helius key | `settings.ts`, `RPC_URL` and `WS_URL` |
| Which wallet pays? | A dedicated keeper wallet, kept at 2 SOL by airdrop | The deploy wallet | `keeper-runner.md`, "The keeper wallet"; `settings.ts`, `KEEPER_KEYPAIR` and `FLOAT_TARGET` |
| What may it spend? | 0.003 SOL a transaction, 0.01 SOL a market a day, 0.1 SOL a day; warning at 0.5 SOL, stop at 0.1 SOL; no priority fee | Looser caps with no per-market cap | `settings.ts` |
| What happens on failure? | Simulate first; retry at 30 s, 2 min and 10 min, then park until the market changes; shown in Aviary | Logs only; Telegram alerts | `keeper-runner.md`, "Failures"; `settings.ts`, `RETRY_DELAYS` |
| Who keeps keeper tips? | The runner, unwrapped into its float above 0.05 SOL | Swept to the suite treasury | `settings.ts`, `TIP_UNWRAP_AT` |
| Which markets does it cover? | Every market of our strategies, within the caps | Only markets our own wallets created | `keeper-runner.md`, "Which markets" |
| When do payouts and `settle` run? | Payouts in one daily pass at 00:00 UTC; `settle` at most hourly per market | Payouts on every change | `settings.ts`, `DAILY_PASS_UTC` and `SETTLE_INTERVAL` |

tickets.title: Telegram bot for Pipescope
tickets.resolution:
Resolved with the owner on 2026-11-10, in four short rounds.
Spec: [`docs/spec/pipescope-telegram.md`](/spec/pipescope-telegram/); decision record: ADR 0007; landed in #97.

## Answers to the ticket's questions

- **Which commands**: lookups (a market or strategy card with its facts and Canary results, by address or name), trade links, and alerts; in private chats and groups, plus one unfiltered public channel.
- **How a trade is signed**: the bot holds no key and signs nothing. Buy and Sell buttons are plain links to Aviary's market page with the swap filled in (a trade link), and the trader signs there in their own wallet. On a phone, where Telegram's browser has no wallet, the page offers to reopen itself inside Phantom, Solflare or Backpack.
- **Fee and before-signing rules**: unchanged, because it is the same trade box: 0.5% only when paying with a fee mint, the simulation before every signature, the exit-test tick box. The card also states the fees and repeats the "could not sell back" notice above the Buy button.

Also settled: the bot runs inside `terminal-api` (a webhook route and a Cloudflare Queue), buys nothing and makes no paid call; it stores a chat's id, settings and watch list and nothing about a person or a wallet; strategy and token metadata stay untrusted text that can never become a link in a message.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is the owner's default and can change; "where" is the section of the spec that holds it.

| # | Question | Answer | Alternatives weighed | Where it lives | How it would change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | How is a trade that starts in Telegram signed? | In Aviary's own trade box, reached by a trade link | A Mini App inside Telegram; a link that opens the wallet with the transaction ready | Trading from Telegram; ADR 0007 | Spec and a new build (a Mini App can be added beside the links) |
| 2 | What is in the first version? | Lookups, trade links and alerts | Lookups and trade links only; alerts only | First version | Spec |
| 3 | Which events alert? | New strategies and new markets; for what a chat watches, upgrades and changed Canary outcomes | New listings only; watched changes only | Alerts, What is sent | Spec |
| 4 | Where does the bot work? | Private chats and groups, with Telegram's privacy mode on | Private chats only; inline mode too | Private chats and groups | Spec and BotFather settings |
| 5 | Where is the amount chosen? | In the trade box; `/buy` and `/sell` can fill it in | Preset amount buttons in chat; commands only | Buy, Sell and Trade | Spec |
| 6 | Do the fee and before-signing rules change? | No; the card repeats the fees and the exit-test notice | A card that repeats neither; a separate rate for bot trades | Trading from Telegram | The rate is the API's fee configuration; the card is spec |
| 7 | When is a new-market alert sent? | After the market's first Canary run, at most 5 minutes later | At once and edited later; at once with the results as a reply | Alerts; One place for every value | A value in the bot's config module |
| 8 | When is an upgrade alert sent? | At once, then the results as a second message | Only after Canary finishes; at once only | Alerts, What is sent | Spec |
| 9 | Does the bot know a trader's wallet? | No: no address asked for or stored | Lookups by pasted address; a saved address for alerts on holdings | First version; What the bot stores | Spec |
| 10 | Does the bot show the explanation? | Its summary under the pages' label, with a link to the rest; it never has one made | A link only; the whole explanation in chat | The explanation | Spec |
| 11 | Is there a public channel? | Yes: every new strategy, new market and upgrade, unfiltered | No channel; decide at mainnet | The channel | A var of `terminal-api` |
| 13 | When is it built? | Alongside Aviary's web pages | After the terminal ships; before mainnet only | When it is built | Ticket order |

Limits chosen as defaults without a question, each in the bot's config module: a watch list of 100 a chat, 20 lookups a minute a chat, lists of 10, sending at most 25 messages a second, a group's admin list kept 5 minutes, alerts off for a new chat.

## For the build

- Owner task before the bot's first build ticket: create the working bot in BotFather (privacy mode on, inline mode off, groups allowed) and a private working channel with the bot as an admin.
- Four things the documentation did not settle are listed in the spec as checks for the build to run first ("Checked facts and open checks").

tickets.title: Cut the lending pool's build tickets
tickets.decision: the spec was complete but for withdraw mode, whose thresholds are now measured against the larger of the market's lent value and its target lent value, so a market that has redeemed everything does not lend straight back into the crunch; twelve `build` tickets in one chain: our Kamino lending market on devnet first, then the program slice by slice, each verified in LiteSVM and by a local demo run on devnet's own router and klend bytes, hardening before the first deploy, and a devnet ticket that deploys, registers and runs the demo market against the real Kamino Lend; `rebalance` is called by the demo script and Aviary's form until the keeper runner exists ([resolution](/25/), [spec](/spec/lending-pool/#build-tickets))
tickets.resolution:
**Answer.** `docs/spec/lending-pool.md` and the bar in `docs/spec/README.md` were complete enough to build from, with one gap, settled with the owner today, so no new decision ticket was needed.
The lending AMM (the lending pool's name since [Product and suite names](/17/)) is cut into twelve build tickets labelled `build`, one session each, with native blocking, listed in run order in the spec's [Build tickets](/spec/lending-pool/#build-tickets) and in the map's `## Next`.

**The gap.** Withdraw mode was measured against the market's current lent value, which is 0 once the market has redeemed everything, so the next `rebalance` would leave withdraw mode at once, lend 80% back into the same crunch and re-enter.
The owner chose to measure both thresholds against the larger of the lent value and the target lent value.
The spec's [Withdraw mode](/spec/lending-pool/#withdraw-mode), constants, invariants and test list say so now (merged in #89, with a follow-up in #92).

**The tickets, in run order**

1. Lending AMM: our Kamino lending market on devnet: unblocked, on devnet; it proves Kamino Lend on devnet does what the spec assumes (layout parity, the cToken path, a test borrower, emergency mode) before any program depends on it.
2. Lending AMM: markets that trade from their own vaults: waits for the first ticket and for Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run and Tax AMM: create a tax market.
3. Lending AMM: klend fixtures, and valuing the lent side from Kamino's reserve
4. Lending AMM: lend the surplus with `rebalance`
5. Lending AMM: redeem a swap's shortfall from Kamino inside the swap
6. Lending AMM: remove liquidity in cash or in kind, and lock LP shares
7. Lending AMM: withdraw mode and Kamino's other states
8. Lending AMM: seeding by a launchpad
9. Lending AMM: the fuzzer against a moving Kamino, and the proofs completed
10. Lending AMM: hardening
11. Lending AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market: the end of the program's chain.
12. Lending AMM: Aviary panel, forms and explainer facts: after the deploy, and held by Cut Pipescope's build tickets until Aviary's own tickets exist to block it.

Each one is blocked by the one before it, because they all change the same program.

**How they are verified**

- Tickets 2 to 10: LiteSVM through the real router copied from devnet and klend's deployed bytes, with the `mainnet` build on cloned mainnet reserves and the `devnet` build on accounts dumped from our devnet lending market; and a local demo run of the demo script on a local validator running devnet's router and klend, as `docs/agents/build-tickets.md` asks.
- Tickets 1 and 11: on devnet itself, against the real Kamino Lend there. Ticket 11 runs every check under "On devnet" in the spec's Done means: the market created, funded and rebalanced into Kamino, a sell that redeems in the swap, a test borrower bringing withdraw mode on and off, and emergency mode on and off.
- Every ticket cites the bar's sections in its acceptance criteria, and the program tickets share one block of standing criteria (one config module, both cluster builds, proofs, the fuzzer, compute ceilings, `pipeline-check` clean, decision IDs in the PR).

**What the tickets do not build**

- The keeper runner: until [Keeper runner](/45/) is specified and built, `rebalance` is called by the demo script and by anyone from Aviary's form.
- Anything on mainnet.

**Also changed in the spec**

- Our devnet Kamino reserve gets a second depositor (at least 5 SOL from the devnet wallet), because a reserve holding only our markets' deposits would sit below withdraw mode's entry threshold.
- The `init` form's one possible shape under Pipeline's metadata schema at `5ad130d`: the other mint, then the lent mint, with `lent_index` 1.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is the owner's default, and he may change any of them.

1. **What are withdraw mode's thresholds measured against?**
   Answer (owner, 2026-11-10): the larger of the market's lent value and its target lent value; enter below 5 times, leave above 10 times.
   Alternatives: the target lent value alone; the lent value alone, as first written, which flapped.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Withdraw mode" and "Constants"; in code, build-time constants and one function in the program's config module.
2. **When does the lending AMM's hardening ticket run?**
   Answer: before the first devnet deploy, so the program registered with Pipeline is the hardened one, as for the buy wall AMM.
   Alternative: last, after the deploy, as the bar words it and as the tax AMM does.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Build tickets"; it changes ticket order only.
3. **How are the lending AMM's feature tickets verified?**
   Answer: in LiteSVM and by a local demo run, both on devnet's own router and klend bytes; on devnet itself in the first and the eleventh ticket.
   Alternative: a devnet deploy and upgrade in every ticket.
   Where: `docs/spec/lending-pool.md`, "Build tickets"; it changes acceptance criteria only.
4. **What is the lending AMM's devnet demo market?**
   Answer: WSOL lent, a fresh test token with no authorities, an LP fee of 30 bps, at least 0.5 SOL on the lent side.
   Alternative: a market lending test USDC.
   Where: the first and the eleventh ticket; script parameters.

## For the owner

- The first ticket can run now; it needs devnet SOL only (about 5 SOL sits in our reserve as the second depositor's deposit and can be taken back).
- The twelfth ticket's hold on Cut Pipescope's build tickets should become real edges when Aviary's tickets are cut; a note there asks for it.
- The bar still says each program's last build ticket is its hardening ticket; the buy wall AMM and the lending AMM harden before their first deploy, and the tax AMM after it. One line in the bar could settle which it is.
- The twelfth ticket leaves the lending AMM's explanation pending your approval, since generating it is a paid call.

tickets.title: Cut the containment hook and tax AMM build tickets
tickets.decision: both specs were buildable once the tax AMM's file gained what the bar asks of each product (compute ceilings, invariants, warns, its place in Aviary); 18 build tickets, the tax AMM's eleven first and the hook's seven each after the tax AMM ticket it builds on; verified locally first with devnet last, deployed and then hardened; Canary reports a refused wallet-to-wallet transfer as a warn for any token; policy values in one config module per program, the mint allowlist in one shared crate ([tax AMM spec](/spec/tax-amm/#building-it), [hook spec](/spec/containment-hook/#building-it), build ticket rules)
tickets.resolution:
Yes: `docs/spec/tax-amm.md`, `docs/spec/containment-hook.md` and the bar in `docs/spec/README.md` are complete enough to build both from, once the small gaps below were filled and four questions were put to the owner.
No new decision ticket was needed.
Everything landed in #90, with a follow-up in #93.

### The build tickets

18 tickets, labelled `build`, sub-issues of the map, wired with native blocking edges, one session each.

Tax AMM, the first product to build:

1. Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run
2. Tax AMM: create a tax market
3. Tax AMM: seed a market and trade it with buy and sell tax
4. Tax AMM: pay the tax out with distribute
5. Tax AMM: the tax authority
6. Tax AMM: seeding from another program
7. Tax AMM: proofs of the pricing, tax and split maths
8. Tax AMM: invariant fuzzing across every instruction
9. Tax AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and create a demo market
10. Tax AMM: hardening ticket
11. Tax AMM in Aviary: the launch form and the tax panel

Containment hook:

1. Containment hook: bind a token to its home market
2. Containment hook: a contained token moves only through its home market
3. Containment hook: unlock by the goal or the deadline
4. Containment hook: invariant fuzzing of contained tokens
5. Containment hook: deploy on devnet and launch a contained token
6. Containment hook: hardening ticket
7. Containment hook in Aviary: the containment panel and the Unlock button

- Tax AMM tickets 4 to 7 can run side by side after ticket 3; its devnet ticket waits for the proofs and the fuzzing; hardening follows the deploy.
- Each hook ticket is blocked by the tax AMM ticket it builds on: binding by market creation, the allow rule by trading and payouts, fuzzing by the tax AMM's fuzzing harness, the hook's devnet ticket by the tax AMM's.
- The two Aviary tickets are blocked by Cut Pipescope's build tickets as a stand-in, since Aviary's own tickets do not exist yet; that ticket's session swaps the edge for the real ones.
- Every ticket cites the sections of the bar it covers, and they share `docs/agents/build-tickets.md`.
- Not ticketed, as asked: offering the tax AMM to Pipeline's own repo.

### What the specs lacked, now in them

- [`tax-amm.md`](/spec/tax-amm/): "In Aviary" (the launch form and the tax panel), the order of the build, where its policy values live, compute ceilings per instruction, seven invariants for the fuzzing layer, the `pipeline-check` and Canary warns, and what is not measured yet. The bar asks each product's file for these and this file had none of them.
- [`containment-hook.md`](/spec/containment-hook/): the order of the build, where its policy values live, the framework (Anchor, native only if `Execute` cannot meet its ceiling), the Canary warns, and a second devnet token unlocked by its goal.

### For other tickets

- Cut Pipescope's build tickets: the owner's Canary decision below amends a row of `pipescope-canary.md`; posted there.

## Decisions open to MetalLegBob

Each is a default he may change. The register (`docs/decisions.md`) has not landed, so they are listed here for it.

**Answered by the owner in this session**

1. **How does Canary report a token that cannot be sent to another wallet?**
   - Answer: a refused wallet-to-wallet transfer is a warn for any token, ours or anyone else's, with the reason and what the buyer got back by selling. `exit_transferred` fails only when a transferred token cannot then be sold, and a refusal never raises the trade box's "could not sell back" notice.
   - Why it came up: every contained token refuses that transfer by design, so every home market would have shown a Canary fail, against the bar's rule that our strategies show none.
   - Alternatives: a warn only when the hook is ours (an exemption for our own product); keep the fail and write an exception into the bar.
   - Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Canary checks"; to be carried into `pipescope-canary.md`'s `exit_transferred` row. Changes by: spec only, until Canary is built.
2. **Where is a program verified before its devnet ticket?**
   - Answer: local first, devnet last. LiteSVM tests through the router's bytes copied from devnet, and the demo script on a local validator running devnet's router; only the devnet ticket deploys and registers.
   - Alternatives: deploy and register from the first ticket and upgrade devnet at every ticket, which shows half-built versions in Pipeline's registry and can strand early demo markets.
   - Lives in: "Order of the build" in both spec files; `docs/agents/build-tickets.md`, "Verify". Changes by: the tickets' wording.
3. **Is a program hardened before or after its first devnet deploy?**
   - Answer: deploy, then harden. The hardening ticket is the program's last, as the bar says, and redeploys and republishes if it changed the program.
   - Alternatives: harden first, so the first registered bytes are already reviewed (the buy wall AMM's tickets were cut that way, so the two products currently differ).
   - Lives in: "Order of the build" in both spec files; the blocking edges of the two hardening tickets. Changes by: two edges and a sentence.
4. **What name does the tax AMM register under?** Asked while Product and suite names was open; that ticket closed during this session, so it registers as Aviary Tax AMM and nothing was decided here.

**Set by this session, not yet put to the owner**

5. **The security contact** in the strategy metadata and the `security.txt`: this repo's private vulnerability reporting page on GitHub. Alternatives: an email address, a handle. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Custom actions and metadata". Changes by: metadata, and a rebuild for the `security.txt`.
6. **The tax AMM's compute ceilings**: 25,000 units for a quote, 60,000 for a swap, and the rest of the table. They are set from what Pipeline's constant-product example costs, not measured; the build measures them. Alternatives: fix them only after measuring. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Compute ceilings" and "Not measured yet". Changes by: spec and one test module.
7. **The tax AMM's seven fuzzing invariants**, derived from its rules. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "Invariants".
8. **The tax AMM in Aviary**: its own launch form in place of the generic `init` form, and what the tax panel shows, gathered from what the spec already promised. Lives in: `tax-amm.md`, "In Aviary".
9. **The containment hook is written in Anchor**, as the bar asks of every program, although the `test-hook` it starts from is native code; native only if `Execute` cannot stay under 10,000 units. Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Starting point".
10. **A second devnet token unlocked by its goal**, beyond the spec's one unlocked by its deadline, so the hook's read of the deployed tax AMM's counter is shown on devnet. Lives in: `containment-hook.md`, "Done means".
11. **Where policy values live**, applying the owner's standing rule: one config module per program for build-time constants (the tax cap, the suite share, the suite treasury and the recipient limit; for the hook the 90-day limit and the tax AMM's program id), creation parameters or `bind` arguments for everything else. The mint extension allowlist is one list in one small shared crate, which the tax AMM, the containment hook and the lending AMM all depend on, as the lending AMM's ticket-cutting session asked (#93); a product with a stricter rule adds it on top. Run order:

1. Buy wall AMM: a market opens: the program generated from Pipeline's Apache-2.0 template at `5ad130d`, the fixed-size market state with its byte offsets, creation, the mint rules and the seed. Waits for Tax AMM: Pipeline's strategy template in our repo, with CI and a local demo run.
2. Buy wall AMM: plain trading through the router
3. Buy wall AMM: the inventory cap
4. Buy wall AMM: the buy wall
5. Buy wall AMM: payouts and recipient handovers
6. Buy wall AMM: seeding by another program: after ticket 2, so it can run beside tickets 3 to 5.
7. Buy wall AMM: the release gate and layout fixtures
8. Buy wall AMM: hardening
9. Buy wall AMM: deploy on devnet, register with Pipeline and run a demo market: the end of the program's chain.
10. Buy wall AMM: Aviary panel and forms: off the chain, after ticket 9 and Aviary's own build tickets.

How the tickets are built:

- **No upgrade can strand a market.** Ticket 1 fixes one 1,024-byte zero-copy layout holding every field the whole spec needs, with a layout version, a zeroed reserve that only gains appended fields, a compile-time size check, and the discriminator written as fixed bytes so renaming a type can never change it. Every later ticket carries a criterion that no field moves. Ticket 7's gate replays every live market against a new build and must refuse test builds that move a field, change the discriminator or change the size. Ticket 9 then runs one real upgrade on devnet through the gate, against the live demo market.
- **Verified end to end.** Each ticket adds its steps to the demo script, run on a local validator with devnet's router, and its LiteSVM tests send the same router transactions a trader would send, against the router dumped from devnet and pinned by hash. Ticket 9 runs every check in the spec's "Done means" on devnet itself.
- **Each new number matches the spec.** Each ticket reproduces its rows of the spec's worked example exactly: the seed in 1, the prices in 2, the trim in 3, the wall in 4 and the settle in 5.
- **Built to the engineering bar.** Every ticket cites the sections of the bar it covers: compute ceilings, Proptest and Kani on the maths, the stateful fuzzer's invariants, `pipeline-check` with no Fail or Warn, CI and `/code-review` at high effort. tickets.title: Pool4 for Solana design
tickets.resolution:
- **Fee**: chosen per market at creation, 0.25% to 3%, never changeable, and always taken in SOL (from the SOL paid in on a buy, from the SOL paid out on a sell), on top of Pipeline's 0.25%.
- **Trim split**: a reward share of 0% to 30% per market goes to one rewards recipient and the rest is burned; all trimmed SOL becomes the buy wall, and tokens the wall buys go through the same split.
- **Staking**: not in v1; a rewards recipient can be a staking program later.
- **Keeper jobs**: four permissionless custom actions, `place_wall`, `settle`, `pay_rewards` and `sweep_fees`. Only `place_wall` tips: the lower of 0.002 SOL and the market's fee rate times the SOL handled, once 0.01 SOL is idle or spent.
- **Containment hook**: optional by design, but not in v1, because [Containment hook policy](/18/) closed during this session with a first version that binds only tax AMM markets. Pool4 for Solana works with plain mints and keeps what a later hook version would need (router-only counters, SOL-only fees and tips, liquidity that can never leave).
- **Parameters**: per market, fixed at creation: the fee, the wall split, the reward share, both recipients, the cap floor (0.1% to 100% of the seeded tokens) and the cap decay (0% to 100% a day). Fixed for every market: the cap starts at the seeded tokens, a buy lowers it by all the room it opens, the buy wall's crawl of about 4% a day behind a lagged reference, and the keeper thresholds. Pipescope's form pre-fills IMD's own launch values.
- **Where it leaves IMD's design**: rates per second, not per block; at most one day of cap decay allowance builds up while idle; no owner powers at all (IMD's owner can close the market and withdraw everything).
- **Markets**: anyone creates one, seeded by a launchpad in one call or created and seeded in one transaction; liquidity is locked for good; nobody controls a market afterwards, except that each recipient may hand its own role to another wallet. The token trades against wrapped SOL, with its mint and freeze authorities removed and only the tax AMM's extension allowlist; exact-in only; bypass refused.
- **Upgrades can never strand a market**: a fixed-size market state with a layout version and reserved space, a release gate that replays every live market against a new build before it deploys, and fixtures of every released layout in CI. Frozen before mainnet.
- **Checked before writing**: the pricing, trim, ratchet, wall and keeper rules ran as an integer model for 3,000 random sequences (about 957,000 swaps) with every invariant holding; the spec's worked example is the model's output, for the build to reproduce exactly.

One correction to what I told the owner while grilling: I said the reward share would wait in the vault until a contained token's unlock.
The hook's spec allows payouts out of a home vault, and its first version does not bind Pool4 for Solana markets at all, so the spec has no such wait; `pay_rewards` stays a separate action so burns never depend on a transfer.

For other tickets:

- [Cut Pool4 for Solana's build tickets](/24/) is unblocked by this ticket; a suggested slicing is posted there.
- The keeper runner (the map's "Not yet specified") has Pool4 for Solana's part: the four jobs and when to run each, in the spec's "For the keeper runner".
- `docs/spec/README.md` lists its product files but not yet this one, the containment hook's or the lending pool's.
